body: What is the motivation of using a `<div>` instead of `<ul>`? I would keep the `<ul>/<li>` and rename `rootClass` to `listClass`.
I would not use a `{{href}}` variable here, rather put `#` or remove the link, no?

Yes I should have commented earlier.

So the motivation is that `<ul><li>` have a default CSS most of the time: bullet points.

And in most situations you will want to remove the bullet points for styling. So I thought (and that was the case for my demo) that the easiest was just to use `<div>` everywhere.

But we can rollback to `<ul><li>`

I would like the `{{href}}` to be given to every "refinement list" or "refinement link", so that you can generate real links and ctrl+click them or middle click them etc. Right now not implemented I agree. what do you think?
Since you're not using ul and li anymore, you probably should update this part of the documentation :)

body: No preference, I just use .bind because I did not have to use lodash until here. With babel/ES6 a LOT of lodash is "useless" (on a feature side) to us.

In fact here it's required by ES6, Sylvain asked the same question. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Functions/Arrow_functions

I agree this is a bit surprising.

"Because curly braces are used to denote the function’s body, an arrow function that wants to return an object literal outside of a function body must wrap the literal in parentheses. For example"

https://www.nczonline.net/blog/2013/09/10/understanding-ecmascript-6-arrow-functions/
